tasks.task:
Close these in r20; no id/envelope changes; blocker if impossible. Round 9 of the reset 9-11 loop budget.
1 C1 HIGH component-wise resolution: the r19 chain walk resolves each relative target by lexical join plus Clean, which does not resolve symlinked directories before applying .. components. Counterexample: /s/sub/alias -> /s/deep, five conforming snapshot quarantines q1..q5 with q5 oldest, and snapshot.json -> sub/alias/../q5. Filesystem resolution reaches /s/q5; lexical Clean yields /s/sub/q5, absent, so protection misses q5 and retention deletes it, dangling the moved link. Replace lexical-only resolution with a component-wise resolver: split the target, resolve symlinks at each path component as they are traversed, apply .. against the resolved parent, and continue; handle loops (ELOOP/revisit), missing components, escaping the state directory, and non-conforming/directory final targets by terminating that branch harmlessly while recording every visited link entry's identity and cleaned path. State the resolver's exact rules (component order, symlink-at-component behavior, .. after a symlinked directory, absolute targets, path length/loop bound) and keep the complete-chain protection and entry-identity candidacy. Add AC1-10 subcases: (b-alias) the counterexample above (q5 preserved, q4 evicted, link moved, read-through); (b-alias2) alias directory plus a two-component parent traversal; (b-alias-loop) alias cycle terminates harmlessly. Do not weaken R2 or the survivor bound.
2 C7 HIGH recovery-orphaned configured link: the L2 oracle stops before the startup consequence. Corrupt regular snapshot.json plus prompts.json -> snapshot.json: snapshot recovery moves the target; prompts recovery intentionally leaves the now-dangling prompts link untouched; admission publishes a fresh catalog at snapshot.json; the prompts link then resolves to catalog bytes and unchanged SavePrompts rejects LoadPrompts of those bytes, so fresh prompt persistence is blocked and R9's self-healing promise fails, potentially with repeated persistence warnings. Specify a design that reconciles a configured family link orphaned by another family's move with self-healing inside startup recovery, preserving no-overwrite. The design must distinguish (i) originally dangling configured links from (ii) links that dangle only because this run moved their target, state which is in scope and why, define detection (pre-pass resolution identity of each configured path and link status recorded before pass 1), the exact pass ordering and rename decision, the resulting warning record(s) and family attribution, and the post-admission state. Add oracles: revised AC1-10(b-xB2) and an inverse-direction subcase, asserting startup exit 0, fresh valid snapshot.json, fresh prompts state that SavePrompts can persist, exact warning counts, and second-run no-op with no new quarantine. Do not assume owner approval: record the affected-owner confirmation for this semantics as an open checkpoint in section 9.11 rather than claiming it.
3 CR19 L-1 LOW wording: AC1-3's statement that a conforming symlink resolving into a protected target is not itself protected is overbroad; add 'that is not itself a recorded chain element'.
4 CR19 L-2 LOW count formula: the stated deletion formula yields zero for a mixed protected/unprotected layout; state ordinary count = pre-existing minus four and mixed count = the full unprotected set, preserving the operative rule and AC counts.
5 CR19 L-3 LOW oracle: seed a pre-existing conforming symlink resolving into a protected target and assert oldest-first eviction past it (no over-protection).
6 CR19 L-4 LOW editorial: remove the stray backtick in R2 and correct the LoadPrompts branch anchors in section 3 to store.go:95-96 decode, :98-99 trailing, :101-102 Validate, :104-106 checksum.
Return the full nine-section spec, unchanged ids, and a change log mapping each finding to its closing text.
